courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: The Artistic Temperament
courses.description: Class examines how to advance and sustain artistic production, focusing not only on being a successful artist, but also on the importance of creativity and hard work in any successful venture. Honors version available.

source.text: ARTS 50. | 3 Credits. | FY-SEMINAR, FC-AESTH or FC-CREATE.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Time, A Doorway to Visual Expression
courses.description: This class will study one of the lesser considered, but most intriguing, visual components: the element of time.

source.text: ARTS 59. | 3 Credits. | FY-SEMINAR, FC-AESTH or FC-CREATE.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Stories in Sight: The Narrative Image
courses.description: This class looks at the theory and practice of telling stories through photographs.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: The Visual Culture of Photography
courses.description: This course will investigate how photography is inextricably entwined in our lives and histories.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Please Save This: Exploring Personal Histories through Visual Language
courses.description: This class will investigate the idea of personal histories in visual art. As a studio class, the course will be organized around several art making projects. As a catalyst to our own art making, we will explore the idea of personal history and memory through readings, as well as looking at contemporary artists whose work functions in an autobiographical framework.

source.text: ARTS 82. | 3 Credits. | FY-SEMINAR, FC-AESTH or FC-CREATE.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Special Topics
courses.description: Content varies by semester.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Two-Dimensional Design
courses.description: Studio course investigates concepts and strategies of two-dimensional image making. Introduces design elements of visual language (line, shape, value, texture, color). Considers the cultural codes that accompany visual information and how they combine with organizational structures to determine a variety of effects, influence responses, and inform meaning. Foundation requirement for studio majors.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Sculpture : Introduction I (Object/Body)
courses.description: ARTS 103 Sculpture: Introduction I (Object/Body) explores materials, methods, processes, and cultural themes in contemporary sculpture. This project-based course focuses on 3D object investigations, encouraging students to experiment with sculptural techniques, tools, and ideas as a visual language that deepens their understanding of the world through art. Students develop aesthetic sensibility, analytical capacity, and fundamental skills in sculptural media. Foundation requirement for studio majors.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Drawing I
courses.description: Working out of an observational tradition, this course provides an introduction to the concepts and techniques of drawing. Paying attention to both representation and interpretation, the course is designed to develop fundamental skills, aesthetic sensibility, analytical capacity, and creative problem-solving in two-dimensional media.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Photography I
courses.description: Focusing on creative digital photography, this course provides an introduction to the concepts and techniques of digital imagery and lens-based media. Includes methods of interpretation, analysis of images, scanning, retouching, color correction, basic composition, and inkjet printing. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Video I
courses.description: This foundation course introduces students to narrative and non-narrative moving image art through video, sound, and various software programs. Students will learn video production by filming and editing video. Through readings, discussions, screenings, and engagement with artists, projects are designed to develop an understanding of dialogues pertaining to the use of video in contemporary art. Foundation requirement for studio majors.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Sonic Arts 1
courses.description: Sound is a physical vibration and an element of perception central to contemporary art, the transmission of information, and our sense of time, place, and space. This interdisciplinary course tunes students toward practices of listening, introduces the fundamentals of audio recording and production in the arts, and engages contemporary sound art and artists working with sound in installation, sculpture, and video. Students will develop sonic literacy by engaging with concepts, artworks, and the material world through the creation of sonic works, site-visits, and reading and discussion activities. Prior experience in sound or music production is not required.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Darkroom Photography I
courses.description: Introduction to black and white photography in the darkroom through photograms, pinhole, and SLR cameras, processing film, and making gelatin silver prints. Concepts are developed through making, reading and writing, engaging with established and historical artists, and critiquing peers' work. B&W process and aesthetic is approached as tradition, genre, abstraction.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Graphic Design as a Tool for Art-making
courses.description: This course introduces students to the essential principles and practices of graphic design while developing technical proficiency in industry-standard digital tools. Students will learn to create content from various digital platforms, then transform their digital work into tangible forms through various physical production methods including inkjet printing, vinyl cutting, router and/or laser cutting. Through hands-on projects such as stencil design, wood objects, flag design, banners, and experimental zines-students will master fundamental design concepts such as vector graphics, comprehension of visual hierarchy, layout design, typography principles, color theory, and visual communication.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Collage: Strategies for Thinking and Making
courses.description: Collage is both an artistic technique and a way of thinking. Even though its historical roots stem from the early 20th century, it is an image-construction strategy that is almost ubiquitous today. Using a variety of conceptual and media approaches, this course explores strategies of collage in contemporary studio practice.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Digital Drawing I
courses.description: This class delves into the convergence of traditional drawing and technology by harnessing the capabilities of powerful drawing apps like Adobe Fresco and others, utilizing the graphic tablet as a primary tool to replicate natural mediums. Beyond technical proficiency, the course critically examines how new media perpetually influences traditional studio practices, providing valuable insights into contemporary methods of artistic production. Please note that the class exclusively covers iPad versions of drawing applications, excluding mobile apps like Procreate for iPad or Clip Studio for Android. Owning a personal iPad is not a prerequisite for enrollment.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Painting I
courses.description: Recommended preparation, ARTS 104 . This course will introduce the fundamentals of painting and various painting techniques through studio lab activity, lectures, demonstrations, and discussions. The course intends to guide students through developing their technical, formal, conceptual, and creative sensibilities to the painting process.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Sculpture II
courses.description: An expansion on the foundations of three-dimensional artwork as taught in Sculpture I. Students will continue the research and 3D art making through materials, process and context through the application of the various sculpture media.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Photography II
courses.description: Continuation of ARTS 105 with continued focus on advanced creative digital photography techniques.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Video II
courses.description: In this intermediate-level class students expand on video production skills including lighting techniques, blocking and staging, and sound recording. Students learn advanced post production skills including sound design, color grading and further develop skills in continuity editing and non-narrative forms. Students will deepen their creative process and artistic strategies through research and writing to develop projects, and learn how to work collaboratively.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, ARTS 106; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Sonic Arts 2
courses.description: This intermediate-level course builds upon the foundations of audio recording and production introduced in Sonic Arts 1. Students will expand their sonic literacy through advanced production and post-production practices, including mixing for various spaces, creating multi-channel sound installations, and working with specialized microphones such as hydrophones and contact microphones. The course introduces electrocrafting as a means of exploring non-conventional forms of audio generation and transmission. Through case studies, readings, and discussions, students will refine their creative processes and critical engagement with contemporary arts, culminating in a capstone project that integrates sound and visual or sculptural mediums.

source.text: ARTS 207. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, ARTS 107 . | FC-AESTH or FC-CREATE.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Print I
courses.description: Introduction to four basic approaches to printmaking: intaglio, relief, planographic, and stencil processes. Students will explore creative strategies unique to the printed process.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: 2D Animation
courses.description: This class explores several techniques of 2D character animation, including storyboarding and conceptualizing, pencil testing and timing animation, animating simple sequences with Photoshop, experimenting with coloring and materials under a film camera, and compositing in After Effects.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Ceramic I
courses.description: An investigation of clay as a medium; developing technical skills, aesthetic awareness, and historical perspective.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Life Drawing
courses.description: Through the study of anatomy and observation of the human form, students develop the ability to create powerful, realistic figure drawings. Fundamental skills and concepts include expressive use of line, value, weight, and volume plus classical techniques in shading, gesture, sighting, and composition.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Darkroom Photography II
courses.description: Continuation of ARTS 115 with advanced focus on conceptual topics and techniques of black and white analog photography. This course will provide students with proficiency in the operation of medium and large format cameras and advanced printing techniques. Concepts are developed through making, reading and writing, engaging with established and historical artists, and critiquing peers' work.

source.text: ARTS 215. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, ARTS 115 . | FC-AESTH or FC-CREATE.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Color: Theory and Concept
courses.description: This course explores the intricacies of color theory with regard to perception, systems, and application in visual art. Further, the course considers color as subject and concept in contemporary art. Previously offered as ARTS 121.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Wood Sculpture
courses.description: This class examines wood sculpture from both a technical and intuitive perspective. Students are taught woodworking skills and are then encouraged to use these skills to discover their creative potential.

source.text: ARTS 233. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-CREATE, HI-PERFORM.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Screen Printing
courses.description: Recommended preparation, Any Tier I Studio Art course. An intermediate studio course focused on creating stencil-based print images. Students explore a range of technical approaches and will investigate art making concepts specific to screen printing as well as the intersections of screen printing with other two-dimensional art forms.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Metal Sculpture
courses.description: This class examines metal sculpture from both a technical and intuitive perspective. Students are taught metalworking skills and are then encouraged to use these skills to discover their creative potential.

source.text: ARTS 243. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-CREATE, HI-PERFORM.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Special Topics in Studio Art
courses.description: Required preparation, any introductory studio art course or permission of the instructor. Selected topics in studio art.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Painting II
courses.description: This course aims to continue guiding painting students through developing sensibilities to paint handling, color, composition, and spatial design, with an emphasis on experimentation. Students will develop their work in context to themes that are significant in painting history, relevant to contemporary art, and their personal lens.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Loving Your Local Art Scene
courses.description: This course takes students on a tour of Chapel Hill, Carrboro, Durham, and Raleigh's grassroots visual arts scenes, exploring everything from commercial galleries to artist-run non-profits to craft fairs to artists' studios. We will use our local arts scene as a case study to map out how art worlds function. Students' final assignment is to contribute to an ongoing digital web-based - an interactive local arts map. This class is especially beneficial for student artists.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Ceramic II
courses.description: Continuation of ARTS 213 .

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Narrative Painting
courses.description: Students will explore themes in the vast history of narrative paintings by researching and responding to these themes, and create narrative paintings through their own personal lens. We will explore topics of the genre, from historical works, to how contemporary artists are interpreting and creating narratives that mirror the diverse spectrum of identities, materials, and histories in our lifetime.

source.text: ARTS 322. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, ARTS 202 . | FC-AESTH or FC-CREATE, HI-PERFORM.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Sculpture Garden: Art in the Public and Projects of Scale
courses.description: Sculpture Garden is a theme-based course taught through a faculty-led project as a way to develop interdisciplinary student-centered approaches to large scale/public artworks on campus and beyond. The course is centered on the Alumni Sculpture Garden as a locus for understanding space, place, and large scale contemporary art. Coursework reflects the intellectual and professional missions and research-creations of our faculty, collaboratively engaging these skill sets, from ideation to execution in projects and research presentation of scale.

source.text: ARTS 323. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-CREATE, HI-PERFORM.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Drawing II
courses.description: This class builds on predominantly perceptually based concepts of basic drawing and introduces abstraction, interpretive, and conceptual drawing strategies. Class assignments develop understanding of the language of drawing and provide a foundation that aims to support independent investigation and personal approaches to drawing's unique capabilities.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: MAKE: Art in the (New) Age
courses.description: Suggested preparation, ARTS 103 . This course examines the connecting trajectories of artistic and technological developments from early modernism to the contemporary. While addressing the interconnected nature of technology, technique, craft and art, students will work with our new technologies (Laser and Vinyl Cutter, 3D Printer, etc.) to create 3D work.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Abstract Painting
courses.description: This studio course will explore the vast visual language of abstract painting. Students will examine abstraction through creating paintings within a historical, visual, and cultural framework, and acquire context about the emergence and persistence of painted abstraction.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Phantasmagoria: Haunted Art, History, and Installation
courses.description: This course will be organized around four art making/art building projects, culminating in a class presentation of a multimedia phantasmagoria. Students will research early light/shadow, pre-cinema techniques, hauntings/horror and artists whose work is influenced by these tropes. We will work with Maker's Spaces to produce components for this course. Previously offered as ARTS 253.

source.text: ARTS 353. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-CREATE, HI-PERFORM.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: The Practice of Representation: Portraiture in Photography
courses.description: This course examines the practical and theoretical issues of portraiture. Students will learn technical skills and conceptual strategies to engage with issues of representation and notions of identity. We will explore the history of the photographic portraiture as well as work of contemporary portrait artists working in a post-modern age.

source.text: ARTS 355. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, ARTS 105 . | FC-AESTH or FC-CREATE.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Letterpress
courses.description: This class explores the concepts and craft of letterpress printing. Technical skills include typesetting, linoleum carving, and digital interfaces for making image and text matrices. Projects explore the special relationship of image and word and are designed around specific text/image forms: broadside, poster, portfolio, and book.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: At the Radical Edge of Life: Art, Space, and Ecology
courses.description: Art at the Edge of Life: Art, Space, and Ecology is a course organized around 2-3 art making/art building projects, culminating in a class presentation of a final public art installation. Part seminar and part studio, students will research early ecology, sustainability, green movements and artists whose work is influenced by these tropes. We will work with BeAM and with experts in the field to find solutions for the issues that we face today.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: The Walking Seminar: A Territorial Investigation
courses.description: Recommended preparation, ARTS 104 . This seminar engages students in a territorial investigation of the North Carolina landscape. Meandering through the landscape we will explore different art mediums while simultaneously fostering an appreciation for the natural environment. Through hiking and backpacking students will foster a means for understanding their location and documenting their experience.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Print II
courses.description: This course continues an investigation of print techniques and concepts. Projects develop an understanding of print strategies, focusing on the affordances of processes unique to printmaking. This approach positions traditional techniques as a point of departure for seeking an expanded definition of printmaking.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Art, Rites and Rituals of Pilgrimage
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the culture, history and contemporary context of pilgrimage and the Camino de Santiago through the lens of performance art and other embodied aesthetic experiences. Several performative projects form the core of the coursework with the Camino de Santiago-specifically, the Camino Francés, becomes the site and our studio for both cultural and artistic purposes.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: States of Change
courses.description: This course will investigate the idea of a lived practice. As a class in studio arts, the course is organized around several perspectives on what it means to be rooted in social engagement. As a catalyst to our own art making and understanding of our mediums and fields, we will explore the proximity of art and social action and the utility of social engagement through service-learning projects set in the global landscape.

courses.title: Advanced Painting Projects
courses.description: This course focuses on the historically rich practice of painting, and is designed to guide the advanced painting student through the research, conceptual, aesthetic, and technical components of a comprehensive studio practice, and developing and maintaining a studio work ethic.

courses.title: Art and Science: Merging Printmaking and Biology
courses.description: This class explores the intersection of two disciplines, art and science. Research skills intrinsic to both include curiosity, close observation, experimentation, and visual analysis. Organized around printmaking projects informed by specific topics in biology, students adapt theory and practical skills from both disciplines to create artworks using several printmaking techniques. Permission of the instructors. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Performance as Social Practice: Exploring Artistic Expression and Social Change
courses.description: This course introduces the politics of performance art and its implications on social practice. Through a blend of seminar discussions, group workshops, and critique sessions, we will delve into various strategies for engaging with the medium. Our exploration will involve careful consideration of decolonial gestures, materiality, space, context, and intentionality. We'll analyze how contemporary artists navigate discourses surrounding race, gender, sexuality, nationality, and class. Active participation in reading discussions, exercises, and artist lectures is mandatory.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Conceptual-Experimental Photography
courses.description: An advanced photography course for students interested in contemporary photographic practices, critical theory, art history, and experimental processes: theory and practice, formal and conceptual investigations, and historical and contemporary strategies will all be given equal attention.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Advanced Video
courses.description: This advanced level video course focuses on the conceptual development of long-term projects with a focus on advanced production skills. Students will continue to deepen their production and post-production skills through in class tutorials while expanding upon experimental and non-narrative artistic strategies such as multi-channel installation.

courses.title: Book Art
courses.description: Required preparation, one additional two-dimensional studio course (drawing, photography, or printmaking). Defining the book as a "multiple and sequential picture plane," this course considers a range of traditional approaches and conceptual departures of the book as a format for creative expression.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Photo Printmaking
courses.description: This course combines a technical approach (making printing matrices using photographic processes) with a conceptual framework (the photographic "voice" and its interpretation in printmaking). Artmaking projects explore salient ideas such as appropriation versus capture, documentation, truth-telling and fabrication, or narrative invention using specific technical processes such as photogravure and cyanotype.

courses.title: Studio Art Practicum or Internship
courses.description: Required preparation, 15 hours ARTS courses. Allows studio art majors to pursue unpaid practicums or internships for credit. Examples include working as a studio assistant or working in art-related fields, such as galleries, design firms, architectural firms, and nonprofit arts organizations. Work undertaken must comply with Federal criteria governing unpaid internships. Departmental approval required.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Senior Professional Practices Seminar
courses.description: This course is a capstone course for the studio art major. Appropriate for BFA students and BA students who anticipate careers in fine art and art adjacent fields (e.g. design.) Topics covered include issues of professional development, curatorial practice, and presentation of works of art in exhibition. The culminating project is mounting the Senior Exhibition. Restricted to senior studio art majors.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Movie Making Machines: Learning About Cinema in the Maker Space
courses.description: This projects-based seminar will introduce students to the fundamental optical and technological principles of motion pictures. By using the Maker Space to design and fabricate pinhole cameras, zoetropes, and 16mm film strips, students will gain a deep understanding of the material and technological foundations of the cinema, and the operating principles that are behind not only the classic films of Hollywood's past, but the high-definition digital imaging technologies of the present.
